tabPolicy.T1 path segment: Tabs drawn as LINKS (nav + a[aria-current]) whose tabs have their own screen IDs, under a persistent record/section header, at a level with no dynamic sibling segment. Applied: Student hub (ST-05/06/07/10 + Assessment tab), Faculty assessment record (FA-08…12), Super Admin Content (SA-10/SA-12) and Operations (SA-18/20/22). All match proposedRoute.
tabPolicy.T2 ?tab= query: Link-tabs with own screen IDs on a COLLECTION page whose path already has a dynamic child (/x/[id]): a static tab segment would take a name from the id namespace, and the parent's children would stop sharing a prefix with the tab. Default tab has no parameter (the bare URL renders it). Applied: ST-04, FA-04, FA-14 drafts (added), IA-06/08/13/15, IA-16, IA-18. All match proposedRoute except FA-14 (parameter added) and IA-06 (canonical URL is the bare /institute/people; the proposed ?tab=students still resolves).
tabPolicy.T3 optional view query: role=tablist buttons, segmented toggles or filter links that switch views of ONE list and have no screen ID of their own: optional query parameter (?show= / ?status= / ?tab= / ?view=) used only for deep links and Back; default omitted. Applied: ST-11, FA-11, FA-12, IA-20, RV-05, CM-04, SA-06, SA-10, SA-12, SA-16, SA-18, SA-20. SA-16 keeps its proposed ?tab= name because it is a screen-level tab set in screens.json; its default tab (vendors) carries no parameter.
tabPolicy.T4 not a tab: Where the board draws a section or an in-page anchor rather than a tab control, no tab URL is created: VE-13 is the #history section of VE-07 (proposed ?tab=history departs, board-forced).
tabPolicy.Departures from proposedRoute: FA-14 gains ?tab=drafts (T2); CM-04 gains ?tab= (T3); IA-06 and SA-16 drop the default-tab parameter from the canonical URL while the proposed form still resolves (T2 / T3); VE-13 loses ?tab=history (T4, board-forced). No path tab was converted to a query tab or vice versa.

stepPolicy.S1 named step slugs: Every guided flow that is URL-addressable carries its step as ?step=<slug>: a lower-case keyword of the drawn stepper label, in drawn order (the Vendor editor keeps its proposed slugs course|formats|preview|submit). Numbers are not used because steps can be inserted or skipped (pre-fills). Departures: FA-07 '?step=1…4' -> experiment|rules|questions|preview (B4-04 stepper); IA-05 '?step=1…' -> experiments|students|review (B2-05 stepper, 3 steps); PU-08 gains ?step=details|review (B1-07 Step 2-3); VE-09 /edit gains ?step= (PROPOSED query; default = the step where the Vendor stopped).
stepPolicy.S2 before / after first save: A wizard that creates a record lives at /<collection>/new?step=<slug> until the record exists, then router.replace() to /<collection>/[id]/edit?step=<slug> so Back never returns to an unsaved form. Revision of a returned record uses /<collection>/[id]/revise?step=<slug>. Applied to the Vendor editor (VE-03…06, VE-08, VE-09; B5-03 'The ID is given on first save'; engine next() lets an unsaved experiment reach steps 2-4). FA-07 ends at 'Assessment created' / 'Saved as draft' and continues in the record tabs (FA-08 'Continue setting up'), so no /faculty/assessments/[id]/edit is created (none drawn). IA-05 creates grants only at the end; no edit URL.
stepPolicy.S3 in-page steps: Steps whose state cannot be rebuilt from a URL stay in-page and are not mirrored: FA-16 (drafting), FA-17 and IA-11 (parsed CSV files). Focus moves to the step heading as drawn.
stepPolicy.S4 deep-link fallback: A step URL whose earlier steps have no data falls back to the first incomplete step (not drawn; PROPOSED). Result screens ('Request sent' is the only exception, kept as the path /request-access/sent per proposedRoute) are states of the flow route.

appRouterTreeNotes: **No dynamic root segment.** XS-06 and XS-07 are implemented inside the seven static workspace folders, so nothing can match `/areas/help` or `/requests/not-allowed` (D-12). Each workspace has exactly one role guard, in its top `layout.tsx`.

**XS-06 in place.** The guard keeps the requested URL and renders the signed-in person's own shell with the XS-06 message (breadcrumb 'Not your workspace', 'Back to Home' to their own home, Help to their own `/<base>/help`). The shell is therefore chosen by the session role, not by the URL folder. In `student/` the guard sits above `(shell)` and `(focused)` so ST-13 is guarded too.

**In-shell not found.** Next.js renders only the root `not-found.tsx` for URLs that match no route, so each workspace adds `[...unmatched]/page.tsx` calling `notFound()`. Its own `not-found.tsx` then renders the board-08 workspace variant inside the shell. A catch-all at `/<base>/[...unmatched]` never shadows a static or dynamic child, because more specific routes win.

**Experiment hub.** `experiments/[experimentId]/layout.tsx` holds the record guard, which renders ST-19 for the hub, its tabs, the format pages and feedback: for 'not given', for an unknown or unpublished id (PROPOSED, so existence is not revealed) and, as the interim pending O-07, for 'no longer given' / 'access ended'. The guard never calls `notFound()`; only a child page with an invalid `[format]` value does (section 3.8). The `(hub)` group adds the header and tabs only to the five tab pages. `(hub)/simulation/page.tsx` and `simulation/web/page.tsx` share the folder name `simulation` in different groups. This is allowed because they resolve to different URLs.

**ST-13 focused layout.** `student/(focused)` and `student/(shell)` both contain `assessments/[assessmentId]`. The dynamic name must be identical in both groups, because Next.js rejects different slug names at the same path level.

**Workspace slugs** are the navigation.json base routes: `/student`, `/faculty`, `/institute`, `/vendor`, `/reviewer`, `/content-manager`, `/admin`. Role ids in code map to these bases. The foundation's `tenant_admin` / 'Tenant Admin' label maps to Institute Admin `/institute`.

**Route-group layout duplication** is kept small. Section headers shared by query-tab or sub-nav pages (IA People, IA Requests, Content access, SA Content, SA Operations) are shared components rendered by each page, not layouts, because no state has to persist between those tabs.
